key_insight: FM² is a federated foundation-model framework that handles both shared and disjoint medical imaging modalities by combining dual expert modules, modality alignment, and caption-based semantic transfer.
clinical_relevance: It could help hospitals train stronger multimodal imaging AI without centralizing patient data, improving adaptability across sites, modalities, and downstream tasks.
method: Trains the core backbone from scratch for medical-domain fidelity, with optional biomedical pretrained encoders for vision-language alignment.
Uses dual Mixture-of-Experts: Class-wise MoE for personalized label knowledge and Domain-wise MoE for shared cross-modality features.
Adds Heterogeneous Modality Alignment plus Caption-Enhanced Learning to transfer knowledge across clients, including disjoint modalities and federated medical VQA.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains on the MIMH benchmark for classification and caption-enhanced learning, plus strong results on real-world medical VQA datasets versus federated baselines.
watch_item: Caption-enhanced learning depends on locally retained GPT-4o-generated captions, so performance and deployment may be sensitive to caption quality, privacy policy, and integration complexity.
paper_title: FM$^2$: Unified Federated Foundation Models for Heterogeneous Multimodal Medical Imaging
